correctness.rationale: The regular dodecahedron vertices split into ten antipodal axes, each inducing one great circle on the normal sphere. The 10 planes are in general position and produce 92 sign chambers and 180 spherical edges. The source exact quadratic-field certificate checks all 1024 sign masks, 90 circle crossing points, all 30 geometric dodecahedral edges, every chamber sign and polygon-side count, and every labeled arc length; it finds 20 chambers of six-sided sections, 60 of eight-sided, and 12 of ten-sided. Boundary edges: 120 six/eight interfaces of length h and 60 eight/ten of length p, with no six/ten adjacency. I independently generated the 20 vertices and 30 edges, sorted 18 intersection arcs per great circle and measured 180 arcs geometrically; it reproduced exact interface counts and both exact lengths to 9e-16. For a short random tangent displacement on the sphere, one-way crossing probability of interface length L is L/(4*pi^2)t+O(t^2), since average positive normal tangent component=1/pi and sphere area=4*pi; finitely many crossing vertices contribute only O(t^2). Thus the coefficients follow. The exact arc identity 2h+p=pi/3 gives 10/pi total change. This is a valid first-order result only, not a finite-angle kernel.

The exact labeled boundary decomposition distinguishes two structurally different exits from octagonal sections, and the absent direct six/ten edge is a meaningful adjacency restriction. final_claim: A Haar-random central-plane dodecahedral section whose normal is rotated by a random tangent geodesic angle t has one-way six-to-eight transition probability 30h/pi^2*t+O(t^2), eight-to-ten 15p/pi^2*t+O(t^2), reverse directions equal at leading order, no direct six-to-ten O(t) edge, and total section-type-change probability 10/pi*t+O(t^2), where h=acos((3+sqrt5)/(4sqrt2)), p=acos((1+3sqrt5)/8).
